# Flow audit — after_ed52cec8

*Generated by `tools/flow-audit.mjs` from `out/flow-audit/after-ed52cec8/samples.jsonl` (sampler: `tools/harness/flow-sampler.mjs`). Build ed52cec8. The rule is UIB_JOB_16: need = 2 s + 0.4 s per word (cap 10 s); a press ends text legitimately; nothing opens on top of what is being read; one voice at a time.*

## How to read this

- **too fast** — a text block that left the screen by itself (no press in the second before) before its need. Lines that arrived together are one block and read together. A text that grew longer (typing) or re-wrapped or is still elsewhere on the same canvas has not left.
- **overlap** — *hidden* / *partly covered*: a text run under a LATER opaque draw in the same canvas frame (a window, card, banner, picture or child canvas blitted over it) that started by itself; *text on text*: two visible texts printing over each other.
- **voices** — three or more distinct places (canvas + a 3×3 cell of it) getting new text within ~4 s, or a guide balloon up while something else is new. Only arrivals no press asked for.
- **stream** — three or more lines arriving unprompted less than 1.5 s apart (the job's "at least 1.5 s per line" for changelogs).
- **guide** — the guide hook (`__guide()` side message, or Lamby's balloon) said a line was active but its text was never drawn on any canvas while it was active. In 1997 the side message is drawn only while the pointer rests on the helper tip (src/desktop/os.ts `guideTipAt`), so an unprompted side message is invisible; Lamby's balloon is the visible one.
- **clock** — a clock text that jumps 20 min or more inside two minutes (rule 4).
- **flicker** — a text that was on screen for 0.6 s or less and left by itself (a blink, a glitch frame): listed so a blinking prompt is not invisible.
- Times are seconds from the start of the sampled walk, **wall-clock**. A "canvas" is an offscreen 2D surface; rects are in that canvas's own pixels (the OS desktop is 512×384, Room 2's workstation 676×390 plus a draw scale, the handset 180×360 at 2×).
- **Not in a failure count:** the by-design EXCEPTIONS (their own table, with the reason), and anything a walker press ended. The tool sees canvas text only, not DOM captions or the pixel games' rect letters, and it cannot know which surface the player is facing.

## The run

- 11334 samples over 47:13 (2833 s), 867 walker presses, 860 walker log lines, 19 canvases seen.
- Frame rate while sampled: median 60 fps, 0.0 % of samples under 12 fps (the piece's clock and the wall clock agree).
- Eras as the walker tracked them (`os.desktopEra`): **1997** 0:01–8:16, **2003** 8:17–17:04, **2016** 17:04–23:06, **2026** 23:06–47:13
- 6937 text lines were seen arriving and 5460 blocks; 2257 lines left earlier than their need, of which a press ended 1810 (not counted); 442 covered/overprinted texts began right after a press (not counted).

## Exceptions in force

Named in `tools/flow-audit.mjs` `EXCEPTIONS`; a hit is reported above, never counted as a failure.

- **2016-cascade** (6 hits) — The 2016 cascade's speed is the point ("outnumbered", s3_maiden.json `cascade`, graceQueueLite CASCADE_STEP): the group's forwards land faster than review can answer, and the piece says so. Only the PHONE's group thread while stage is `takeover` is exempt — the board's PRIORITY ALERT cards, the Review rows and Orla's message are not.
- **2026-clip** (17 hits) — The 2026 clip ("The Great Becoming", Second Thoughts' AI-made video) is timed to its music and narrator, and its cards are the beat (S360/S364, Sérgio 11 Nov: "the sound is fantastic, love the check marks and the intensity of each of the signs"). Its cards stay exactly as timed. Matched by the browser's clip takeover being live, or by the clip's own strings (data/dialog/s4_v3.json `clip`).
- **1997-update-cascade** (7 hits) — The 1997 update arrives as a CASCADE of error windows (and Un-Walk's own notice) that pile on one another and on the desk ("the beat is that there is nothing to fight", src/desktop/apps/update.ts `cascade`; SCRIPT_UPDATE v0.5): windows covering windows is the picture. And 2016's update notice ("Important Changes") over the board, once Lambient's last line has gone and clear of the Handset Window (F06): the era is over, the board is not being read. Only while those updates are up.
- **desktop-icons** (3 hits) — A desktop icon's label under an open window is how a desktop works (1997 / 2003: "Session", "rootcause.", "Family Form", "Care Log"); an icon is not a reading surface, and the window over it is the one in use.
- **2003-redaction** (36 hits) — Restorify blacks out Caleb's thread line by line, and later gives it back line by line (src/desktop/apps/caleb.ts, the redaction walk). The words were on screen and read before it began; the line-by-line removal and return is the system's act on them, and the transcript follows the walk. While it is sealed there is nothing under a window to read; when the words return, the restored history scrolls up under Caleb's new lines (its old lines only — his new ones are held by the rule).
- **2026-ai-acting** (10 hits) — His brief (UIB_JOB_16 Part B): "The banner itself may be brief: it is the AI acting." The green "Second Thoughts is using your computer" bar comes and goes with the AI's act on her computer (browser.ts `act`); and WHILE it acts (N10: it reads her mail, mutes Junie, starts the game) the pages it flips through are its hands moving at a machine's speed — each was hers to read before (the mailbox she lived that morning), and the chat says what it took. Only during the act; the AI's chat lines after it are held by the rule.
- **2016-board-popin** (3 hits) — GracePlatform's own pop-in card over its own board — the kit's URGENT card, Kindredraft's offer, "This week", the Malta alert (F03, now after two members and ~9 s or OK): a modal card is the one voice, and the board under it takes no press while it is up. The Handset Window has its own column and is never under one (F01/F02).
- **1997-irc-modal** (2 hits) — Rob's two one-answer dialogs in the channel (his request to talk, his file) are modal ("you have to accept", S186): the conversation under them waits for the answer, nothing new lands in it while they are up.
- **2003-ending** (1 hits) — Restorify's ending (u3: "Service Transition") opens once Daniel's last line to Caleb has been read (spine RESIDUE_GAP 4.4 s, S369): the conversation is over and nothing more arrives in it; the system takes the screen.
- **2003-strip-foot** (0 hits) — While the Accountability strip is up it docks over the Messenger's FOOT — its tray and the two pictures' captions ("daniel") — and the transcript is drawn above it, its newest line always in view (F07, S369). Likewise his song's player over the top of the window: the transcript starts below it; only Caleb's picture caption ("caleb / my eyes and my") is under it.
- **2026-lightbox** (2 hits) — A screenshot or page SHE opened larger (browser.ts `lightbox`: a press opens it, any press closes it, S364): a viewer over the chat that her own press put there and takes away.
- **2026-site-popup** (2 hits) — The news site's own newsletter box ("Never miss a story") over its MOST READ rail — the 2026 web's furniture (S363, his N5 "2026's web furniture"); the story itself is never under it.
- **2026-ball** (16 hits) — The ball is deliberate stillness, about 3½ minutes with no controls, its lines timed to the audio (memory: stillness-is-not-a-dead-end; src/desktop/apps/ball.ts). Anything drawn while the ball is live is timed by the recording, not by a reader.

## Not checked

- DOM text (captions, the frame's menu, the entrance's own panels): only canvas text is drawn here.
- Which surface the player is facing: a surface behind the head that redraws still counts.
- Sound: whether a voice or a clip overlaps another is invisible here (headless, no audio).
- The walker's press rhythm (about 2.2 s) hides every "too fast" a press ended; the report counts those in the run summary only.
